name: invitations
title: Invitations
description: Invitation links and typed codes for a room, with a payload for a scannable code.

facilities.description: Invitation codes, links, parsing, sharing and scan payload

infrastructure.deployedReason: Local library; no service is deployed by this package. The invite address is the application's own page.

text.purpose: `invitations` makes the link and the short code a person uses to invite others into a room: it generates a code from an alphabet with no look-alike characters, builds a link on the application's invite address that carries the code (and optionally a room), parses such a link back, formats a code for reading out and offers the link through the system share sheet or the clipboard on the web. It supplies the text a scannable-code renderer encodes; drawing the scannable code is a platform call and is not in this component.
text.userInputs: Two settings. `inviteAddress` (address grammar, optional: without it no links are made) is the application's own page that invitation links point to: an absolute http or https address with no credentials, query or fragment. `codeLength` (default 6) is the number of characters in a code.
text.integration: Server: when a room is created call `generateCode(settings.codeLength, random)`, keep it with the room and give it to the directory entry so people can join by code; send `inviteLink(settings, { code, roomId })` in the room's view for clients to show or share. Web: `shareInvitation(link, text, { share: navigator.share?.bind(navigator), writeText: navigator.clipboard?.writeText.bind(navigator.clipboard) })`. All platforms: `parseInvite` on a link the application was opened with. Scannable code: pass `scanPayload(link).text` to the platform's renderer (iOS Core Image `CIFilter.qrCodeGenerator`, level M, as the recipe does; Android and web need a library or service chosen by the application). `examples/consumer.ts` runs the whole cycle without a game.
text.infrastructure: No service. The invite address belongs to the application's web hosting.
text.verification: Required-local: `node --test tests/web.test.ts` checks the address grammar, generation inside the alphabet, normalising and reading-out format, link building and parsing against `tests/fixtures/invites.json`, the scan payload, every sharing outcome and the example. Platform: `python3 tests/native.py apple` compiles and runs the Swift port against the same fixture; `python3 tests/native.py android` compiles the Kotlin port (needs kotlinc, not installed on the authoring machine, so not run there).
text.scenarios: A host creates a room; the screen shows `KT7-Q2P` to read out and a link to share. A guest types `kt7q2p` with different spacing and case and the right room is found. A guest scans the scannable code drawn from the payload and the application opens on the invite address with the code and room filled in. A link from another site, with a wrong-length code or an invalid room id, is ignored.
text.updates: Patch updates replace files; no persisted-state migration. Codes live with the rooms that use them. The link grammar is part of the interface: changing it needs a new interface version.

agentInstructions: Select this component when people join by link, typed code or scannable code. Set `inviteAddress` from the application's own web address (ask the developer; it is not a secret) and keep `codeLength` at 6 unless the room count demands more. Connect it to the room directory (codes) and to the host screens (share and scan). If the application needs a drawn scannable code, choose a renderer for each platform separately.
developerInstructions: Supply the invite address. Decide how a scannable code is drawn on each platform; this component only gives the text. Keep the code with the room record and expose it in the room list. No accounts or keys are needed.
